title: Runbook telemetry slicing and playlet prioritizer
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Problem: oncall and support engineers face long decision trees in runbooks; frequently-used corrective steps are hidden among low-impact instructions. We have rich telemetry (errors, routes, token counts, latency spikes, KV cache hits) but no systematic way to slice that telemetry into actionable "playlets" and prioritize which micro-actions should be surfaced or auto-executed.
acceptance_criteria: Telemetry slicing pipeline produces per-incident playlet candidates with a stable scoring key (urgency, frequency, success-rate) for at least three important incident types (model OOM, degraded latency, auth failures)
Console UI surfaces top-3 prioritized playlets for an ongoing incident with a single-click expand + run experience (API + UI)
API returns prioritized playlets within 40ms for typical incident context payloads (p99 under our canary), falling back cleanly to full runbook if prioritizer fails
Playlet execution supports safe-mode (dry-run), canary rollout (10% org), and audit logging with provenance linked to incident ID
End-to-end tests + regression evals added; rollout plan documented; ops runbook updated with new workflow
implementation_notes: Add a telemetry-slicing job (in ingestion layer) that tags events with candidate playlets and aggregates success/failure stats per playlet signature

Design a lightweight scoring service (stateless API) that computes urgency score = weighted(incidence_rate, recent-failure-rate, mean-time-to-repair) — start with heuristic weights and expose an endpoint for tuning
Extend runbook-as-tasks model to support 'playlet' metadata: safe-guards, required-permissions, estimated-cost, prechecks
UI: add a "Prioritized Actions" panel on incident view; wire a single-run RPC with confirmation modal and TTLed undo token
Telemetry retention: slice job needs 90d window for frequency, 7d window for recency. Use existing metrics pipeline (prometheus->clickhouse) and submit a schema change ticket if needed
Security: ensure KMS-signed audit events for playlet execution and integrate with existing RBAC checks (no execution without permission)
updates: 2026-03-02: Spike completed — mapped telemetry signals to a first set of 18 playlet candidates (OOM eviction, prefix-cache-warm, infra-retry, JWT-refresh). Notes in design doc.
2026-03-05: Chose heuristics-based scorer for MVP instead of ML model to reduce ops complexity. Product agrees to start with tunable weights.
2026-03-09: Backend prototype (scoring service + tagging job) deployed to staging; sample prioritizer API returns top-3 in ~18ms (staging infra)
2026-03-11: UX mockups reviewed by PM and Design; safety modal added per review; integration points annotated for telemetry event IDs
2026-03-12: Began wiring audit logging hooks and dry-run support; flagged permission gating as a blocker for broad rollout
comments: Claire Huang (PM): Recommend we include an escape-hatch that automatically switches to manual runbook if a playlet execution fails twice in a row. Also want an admin toggle for scoring aggressiveness.
Marco Silva (Design): Mockups posted in Figma. Emphasize compactness on single incident pane; avoid interrupting oncall flow. Link: https://www.figma.com/file/abcd1234/playlet-prioritizer
SRE Team (via standup): Concern about 3rd-party dependencies in scoring path — keep scoring stateless and cache results near console to avoid extra RPS to core systems.
Security Review (initial): Ensure playlet prechecks include permission verification and that undo tokens are short-lived. Follow-up required before 50% rollout.
